fix: Use defusedxml, which provides drop-in replacements with entity expansion disabled.

name: YAML parsed with the unsafe loader
message: YAML is parsed with a loader that can instantiate arbitrary objects
why: The default loader honours tags like !!python/object/apply, which constructs arbitrary Python objects and can call arbitrary functions. Loading untrusted YAML is loading untrusted code.
fix: Use yaml.safe_load, or pass Loader=yaml.SafeLoader explicitly.

name: Zip archive extraction without directory traversal protection
message: ZipFile.extractall called without member path filtering (Zip Slip)
why: Calling ZipFile.extractall() without validating member filepaths allows Zip Slip attacks where archives containing '../' paths overwrite arbitrary files outside the target extraction directory.
fix: Validate that each member's filename does not contain '..' and resolves to a path strictly inside the target directory before extracting, or extract members individually with path sanitation.

name: Operating system command executed via shell interpreter
message: Rust Command invokes shell interpreter with formatted or variable command string
why: Executing commands through a shell interpreter with dynamic or formatted arguments allows arbitrary command injection via shell metacharacters.
fix: Pass arguments directly to the executable using .arg() or .args() instead of invoking a shell with -c.

name: Bulk environment variable harvesting
message: All environment variables are enumerated in bulk
why: Iterating std::env::vars() dumps the entire process environment, which typically holds API tokens, database passwords, and cloud keys. This is characteristic of supply-chain telemetry or exfiltration payloads.
fix: Read only the specific environment variables required by your application via std::env::var("NAME").

name: Path constructed with format! string interpolation
message: Filesystem path is constructed using format! string interpolation
why: Interpolating user input directly into file paths allows path traversal (e.g., ../../etc/passwd) to access files outside the intended directory.
fix: Validate that components do not contain path separators or '..', and ensure canonicalized paths reside within the allowed base directory.

name: SQL query constructed with format!
message: SQL query is constructed via format! instead of parameter binding
why: Formatting SQL query strings with format! interpolates untrusted values directly into the query, enabling SQL injection.
fix: Use parameterized queries with bind variables (e.g., sqlx::query("SELECT ... WHERE id = $1").bind(id)).

name: Access to sensitive credential file
message: Sensitive credential file path is accessed directly
why: Accessing private SSH keys, AWS credentials, Kubernetes configs, or Docker auth tokens directly from disk is characteristic of credential harvesting malware. Legitimate applications should use standard identity SDKs or environment injection.
fix: Use standard credential provider chains (such as aws-config) or pass credentials via environment variables rather than reading local user credential directories directly.

name: Predictable temporary file created in system temp directory
message: Temporary file created with predictable path in /tmp or /var/tmp
why: Creating files with static or predictable filenames in shared system directories like /tmp allows malicious local users to pre-create symlinks pointing to target files (symlink attack) to corrupt or steal data.
fix: Use the tempfile crate (tempfile::NamedTempFile or tempfile::tempdir) to generate securely randomized, atomically created temporary files.

name: TLS certificate verification disabled
message: TLS certificate or hostname verification is explicitly disabled
why: Disabling certificate validation allows network attackers to perform man-in-the-middle (MitM) attacks and decrypt or alter traffic.
fix: Remove danger_accept_invalid_certs(true) and add custom CA certificates to the certificate store if private certificates are needed.

name: Insecure random number generator used for sensitive token
message: Non-cryptographic RNG rand::thread_rng or rand::random used for security-sensitive token or secret
why: Default thread_rng in the rand crate is not guaranteed to be cryptographically secure across all platforms and seed states, making tokens generated with it potentially predictable.
fix: Use rand::rngs::OsRng or a dedicated cryptographic key generator (such as ring or rand_core) for security-sensitive tokens and secrets.

name: Anthropic API key in source
message: Anthropic API key committed to source
why: The key bills to your account and has no spend limit of its own.
fix: Revoke the key in the Anthropic console and load the replacement from the environment.

name: AWS access key ID in source
message: AWS access key ID committed to source
why: A live access key grants API access to the account until it is rotated, and git history retains it after the line is deleted.
fix: Rotate the key in IAM now, then load it from the environment, an instance role, or a secret manager. Deleting the line is not enough.

name: AWS secret access key in source
message: AWS secret access key committed to source
why: Paired with an access key ID this is full API credentials. Secret keys cannot be viewed again after creation, so a leaked one is usually the only copy an attacker needs.
fix: Rotate the key pair in IAM, then load both halves from the environment or a secret manager.

name: Environment file tracked in git
message: Environment file with assignments is present in the working tree
why: .env files are the single most common way a real credential reaches a public repository, because the file is invisible in most editors and easy to git add -A by accident.
fix: Add .env to .gitignore, commit a .env.example with empty values instead, and run git rm --cached .env if it was ever committed.

name: GitHub token in source
message: GitHub personal access or app token committed to source
why: Depending on its scopes this token can read private repositories, push code, and alter CI, which makes it a direct path into the build pipeline.
fix: Revoke the token in GitHub developer settings, then use a short-lived Actions token or an app installation token.

name: GitLab token in source
message: GitLab personal access token committed to source
why: A GitLab PAT carries the user's own repository and registry access, including write scopes.
fix: Revoke the token in GitLab access tokens settings and replace it with a CI job token or deploy token.

name: Google API key in source
message: Google API key committed to source
why: Unless the key is restricted by referrer, IP, or API, anyone holding it can bill usage to your project.
fix: Rotate the key in Google Cloud credentials and apply API and application restrictions to the replacement.

name: High-entropy value assigned to a credential-shaped name
message: A high-entropy literal is assigned to a credential-shaped name
why: No provider rule recognized this value, which means it is either a credential for something we do not have a signature for, or a false positive. It is reported as tentative for exactly that reason: confirm it before acting, and do not rotate anything on this finding alone.
fix: If it is a credential, rotate it and load it from the environment or a secret manager. If it is not, add an inline waiver naming what it actually is so the next reader does not have to work it out again.

name: JWT with real claims in source
message: Signed JWT committed to source
why: A committed JWT is a bearer credential that works until it expires, and tokens minted for service accounts frequently do not expire at all.
fix: Revoke the session or key that signed it, and load tokens at runtime rather than committing them.

name: npm access token in source
message: npm access token committed to source
why: A publish-scoped npm token lets an attacker ship a malicious version of your package to everyone who installs it. This is the supply chain attack, not a theoretical one.
fix: Revoke the token at npmjs.com, then publish from CI with a short-lived OIDC-issued token.

name: OpenAI API key in source
message: OpenAI API key committed to source
why: The key bills to your account and has no spend limit of its own.
fix: Revoke the key in the OpenAI dashboard and load the replacement from the environment.

name: Private key in source
message: Private key material committed to source
why: A committed private key undermines every identity it authenticates: TLS termination, SSH access, signed artifacts, or JWT issuance.
fix: Treat the key as compromised. Generate a new pair, rotate everything that trusted the old one, and revoke the old certificate if one was issued.

name: SendGrid API key in source
message: SendGrid API key committed to source
why: Mail-sending credentials let an attacker send phishing that passes your own SPF and DKIM checks.
fix: Revoke the key in SendGrid settings and load the replacement from a secret manager.

name: Slack token in source
message: Slack API token committed to source
why: Slack tokens can read channel history and post as the app or user, which makes them useful for both data theft and phishing.
fix: Revoke the token in the Slack app configuration and rotate it into a secret manager.

name: Stripe live secret key in source
message: Stripe live secret key committed to source
why: A live Stripe secret key can move real money and read customer payment records.
fix: Roll the key in the Stripe dashboard immediately, then load it from a secret manager.

name: Azure managed disk unencrypted or encryption disabled
message: Azure managed disk has encryption settings disabled or missing
why: Managed disks without explicit encryption settings or customer-managed disk encryption sets risk storing virtual machine volume data in plaintext or without required key governance, violating data security compliance standards and baseline confidentiality.
fix: Add an encryption_settings block with enabled = true, or reference a customer-managed Disk Encryption Set using disk_encryption_set_id.

name: Azure NSG rule allows internet ingress on administrative port
message: Azure network security rule allows inbound traffic from * to sensitive port
why: Allowing inbound connections from any source address (*) to administrative or database ports (such as SSH 22, RDP 3389, or PostgreSQL 5432) exposes host services to brute-force attacks and exploitation from the public internet.
fix: Restrict source_address_prefix to specific corporate IP CIDRs, application subnets, or use Azure Bastion / Just-In-Time (JIT) VM access instead of public NSG rules.

name: Azure storage account permits public access
message: Azure storage account allows public access without restricting network rules
why: Enabling nested item public access or internet-wide public network access without network firewall rules allows anonymous callers to query blob containers and download sensitive storage account objects directly.
fix: Set allow_nested_items_to_be_public = false and public_network_access_enabled = false, or configure a network_rules block with default_action = "Deny".

name: CloudTrail is not multi-region
message: CloudTrail sets is_multi_region_trail = false
why: Activity in unmonitored regions is invisible, and operating in an unused region is a standard move precisely because nobody is looking there.
fix: Set is_multi_region_trail = true and enable log file validation.

name: Block volume is not encrypted
message: EBS volume sets encrypted = false
why: Detached or snapshotted volumes carry their data in the clear to whoever ends up holding them.
fix: Set encrypted = true, and enable EBS encryption by default at the account level.

name: Kubernetes control plane endpoint is public
message: EKS API server endpoint is reachable from 0.0.0.0/0
why: The Kubernetes API is the control plane for everything in the cluster, and exposing it to the internet makes every authentication weakness in it globally reachable.
fix: Set endpoint_private_access = true, and restrict public_access_cidrs to your own ranges if public access is required.

name: GCP firewall permits unrestricted ingress to sensitive port
message: GCP compute firewall rule exposes sensitive port (22/3389) to 0.0.0.0/0
why: Permitting ingress traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to administrative ports such as SSH (22) or RDP (3389) allows untrusted internet hosts to reach management interfaces, exposing systems to password brute-force and remote exploit attacks.
fix: Restrict source_ranges to authorized management IP ranges, or connect through Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) TCP forwarding rather than exposing ports directly.

name: Cloud SQL instance allows unencrypted connections or open network access
message: Cloud SQL ip_configuration disables SSL enforcement or allows authorized networks from 0.0.0.0/0
why: Disabling SSL requirements transmits database authentication tokens and data in plaintext over network paths. Permitting 0.0.0.0/0 in authorized networks exposes the database listener directly to automated internet-wide port scans.
fix: Set require_ssl = true in ip_configuration, remove 0.0.0.0/0 from authorized_networks, and enforce private IP access using Cloud SQL Auth Proxy or VPC Peering.

name: GCP storage bucket grants public access
message: GCP storage bucket IAM grants access to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers
why: Granting permissions to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers allows anyone on the internet, or any authenticated Google account holder anywhere in the world, to access the bucket's contents without authorization from your project.
fix: Remove allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers from IAM members. Bind permissions only to specific service accounts, groups, or domain identities.

name: Credential hardcoded in Terraform
message: Attribute {{name}} is assigned a literal credential
why: Terraform source is usually more widely readable than the infrastructure it describes, and the value also lands in state, which is rarely encrypted as carefully as people assume.
fix: Move the value to a variable sourced from a secret manager, and mark the variable sensitive so it stays out of plan output.

name: IAM policy grants dangerous privilege escalation actions
message: IAM policy allows dangerous privilege escalation action combinations
why: Actions such as CreatePolicyVersion, SetDefaultPolicyVersion, AttachRolePolicy, or PassRole alongside compute services allow an identity to bypass intended boundaries and elevate its own permissions to administrator.
fix: Remove direct policy modification actions, attach permission boundaries to prevent escalation, and restrict iam:PassRole to specific role ARNs.

name: IAM policy grants every action
message: IAM policy document allows Action "*"
why: A principal holding this can do anything the account can do, including escalating its own privileges and deleting the audit trail that would show it happened.
fix: Enumerate the actions the workload actually calls. Start from CloudTrail data rather than guessing.

name: IAM policy applies to every resource
message: IAM policy document allows Resource "*"
why: Some actions genuinely require a wildcard resource, so this is not always wrong, but it usually means the policy was written without knowing which ARNs the workload touches.
fix: Scope Resource to specific ARNs where the action supports it, and leave a comment where it genuinely cannot.

name: Instance allows IMDSv1
message: Instance metadata service allows IMDSv1 (http_tokens = optional)
why: IMDSv1 answers any request that reaches it, so a server-side request forgery in the application becomes instance credential theft. IMDSv2 requires a PUT-issued token, which SSRF generally cannot perform.
fix: Set http_tokens = "required" and http_put_response_hop_limit = 1.

name: KMS key rotation disabled
message: KMS key does not enable automatic rotation
why: A key that never rotates means a single compromise covers every ciphertext the key ever produced.
fix: Set enable_key_rotation = true. AWS handles the rotation and keeps old material for decryption.

name: Lambda environment variable holds a credential
message: Lambda environment variable {{name}} holds a literal value
why: Lambda environment variables are visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunction and are stored unencrypted at rest unless a KMS key is configured.
fix: Read the secret from Secrets Manager or Parameter Store at cold start, or configure a KMS key for the environment.

name: Load balancer listener serves plaintext HTTP
message: Load balancer listener uses plaintext HTTP without redirecting
why: Credentials and session cookies cross the network in the clear, and any network position between client and load balancer can read or modify them.
fix: Terminate TLS on the listener, or make the HTTP listener a 301 redirect to HTTPS.

name: CloudTrail log file validation disabled
message: CloudTrail sets enable_log_file_validation = false
why: Without validation digests you cannot demonstrate that the audit trail was not edited after an incident.
fix: Set enable_log_file_validation = true.

name: Security group open to the internet
message: Ingress rule allows traffic from 0.0.0.0/0
why: An internet-wide source range removes the network layer from your defence in depth, leaving whatever the application itself enforces as the only control.
fix: Narrow cidr_blocks to the ranges that actually need access, or reference a source security group.

name: Administrative port open to the internet
message: Security group opens an administrative port to 0.0.0.0/0
why: SSH, RDP, and database ports reachable from the whole internet are found by mass scanners within minutes of going live, and credential stuffing against them is continuous and automated.
fix: Restrict cidr_blocks to your own ranges, or reach the host through a bastion, SSM Session Manager, or a private endpoint instead.

name: Database instance is publicly accessible
message: Database instance sets publicly_accessible = true
why: The database gets a public IP and is reachable from the internet subject only to its security group. Database ports are among the most scanned on the internet.
fix: Set publicly_accessible = false and reach the database from inside the VPC or over a private endpoint.

name: Database storage is not encrypted
message: Database sets storage_encrypted = false
why: Snapshots and the underlying volumes are readable by anyone who obtains them, and encryption cannot be enabled in place later without a snapshot and restore.
fix: Set storage_encrypted = true and specify a customer-managed KMS key where policy requires one.

name: S3 public access block explicitly disabled
message: S3 public access block sets block_public_acls to false
why: This is the account's backstop against an accidentally public bucket. Turning it off removes the control that catches the mistake everyone eventually makes.
fix: Set block_public_acls, block_public_policy, ignore_public_acls and restrict_public_buckets to true.

name: S3 bucket ACL grants public access
message: S3 bucket ACL is {{attrs.acl}}
why: A public bucket is enumerable by anyone, and public-read-write additionally lets strangers store content you will pay for and be blamed for.
fix: Set the ACL to private and serve public objects through CloudFront with an origin access identity. Enable the account-level public access block too.

name: Queue or topic policy allows any principal
message: Resource policy allows Principal "*"
why: Any AWS account, and often any anonymous caller, can invoke the allowed actions. On a queue that means message injection or drainage; on a bucket it means public data.
fix: Name the specific principals, and add a condition on aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn.

name: SQS queue does not enable server-side encryption
message: SQS queue does not configure KMS encryption or SQS-managed SSE
why: Messages traversing and stored at rest in an unencrypted SQS queue are readable by anyone who accesses the underlying storage volumes, violating compliance mandates and exposing sensitive pipeline payload data.
fix: Set sqs_managed_sse_enabled = true for Amazon SQS-managed keys (SSE-SQS), or specify kms_master_key_id with a customer-managed or AWS-managed KMS key.

name: Remote state backend not encrypted
message: S3 state backend does not set encrypt = true
why: Terraform state contains every value the configuration touched, including generated passwords and keys, in plaintext. It is frequently the most sensitive object in the account.
fix: Set encrypt = true, add a kms_key_id, and enable versioning plus a lock table on the state bucket.

name: Load balancer accepts obsolete TLS
message: TLS policy permits TLS 1.0 or 1.1: {{attrs.ssl_policy}}
why: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated, fail PCI-DSS, and carry cipher suites with practical downgrade attacks.
fix: Use a TLS 1.2 or 1.3 policy such as ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06.
